title: A page closes when its ticket or group is handled from any path (GitHub issue #10)
objective: A decision or env page stops waiting for the user as soon as its ticket or group is answered through any command or moves on by itself.
outline: core/pool.py, next to leave_group: close_pages(tx, ref, by, names=None) acks every unread decision/env page whose str(ref) matches (only names in `names` when given) and returns their names. tickets.py: call it after ack_in(tx, page, by) inside the change of _set (ready, cancel), cmd_ready_group, cmd_cancel_group (and per cancelled member), cmd_rerun_group and cmd_release (names = the inbox keys read before the release runs). ticket_creator.py: decide() takes the inbox keys before it acts and, where it calls ack(pool, page, by) today, makes one write that acks --page as today and closes the other pages of N among those keys as 'new --revise' (change only decide() and ack(); user_reset, apply_revised and _revise are changed by a later ticket). ticket_controller.py: start_issuer's change (the ticket), _start_job (the group, kinds regression and fixer), land() (inbox keys taken at its start, closed in the landing change for the group and each landed ticket), set_group() when state == 'cancelled', and close_open()'s cancelled branch. Do not edit advance_groups' loop header, idle_lines or can_still_start: another ticket rewrites those lines.

acceptance: Terms: a page 'of S' is an inbox page whose kind is decision or env, whose acked is not true and whose str(ref) equals S (a ticket id or a group id). 'Acked as X' means acked true, acked_at set (osx.now() format) and acked_by X. A page already acked is never changed; pages of kind created, landed, cancelled and idle are never acked by these rules; the acks write no event on tickets or groups.

`tickets.py ready N` (a stuck ticket): in the same pool write that readies N, the page named by --page keeps today's acked_by (--by, else 'answer') and every other page of N is acked as 'tickets ready'. Case: stuck #1 with decision pages p1 and p2 and env page p3, all ref '1', and decision page p4 of ref '2' (stuck #2): `tickets.py ready 1 --page p1 --by alice` exits 0; p1 acked_by 'alice', p2 and p3 acked as 'tickets ready', p4 unread; the pool has exactly one new commit.
`tickets.py cancel N` (a ready or stuck ticket): the same, the other pages acked as 'tickets cancel'.

`tickets.py ready gN`, `tickets.py rerun gN` and `tickets.py cancel gN`: every page of gN other than --page is acked, in the action's own write, as 'tickets ready', 'tickets rerun' and 'tickets cancel'; `cancel gN` also acks, as 'tickets cancel', every page of each member ticket it cancels.

`tickets.py release gN` (a landed group whose release failed): every page of gN that existed when the command started is acked as 'tickets release' (--page keeps --by, else 'answer'), whether the re-run passes or fails; the decision page a failed re-run writes stays unread.

`ticket_creator.py --revise N --from user|main --decision retry|cancel`, and `--decision revise` when it ends ready (exit 0) or escalated (exit 3): every page of N that existed when the command started is acked as 'new --revise' (--page keeps --by, else 'answer', as today); a page the command itself writes (the escalation's question) stays unread; an unusable opener answer (exit 1) and every refusal ack nothing, as today.

Superseded, acked_by 'superseded', written by the controller: (a) when it sets a ready ticket N to running (dispatch), every page of N; (b) when it starts a regression or a fixer job for gN, every page of gN; (c) when it lands gN, every page of gN and of each ticket that lands, if the page existed when that landing began - the push-failed decision page the landing itself writes and the pages written after it (release failed) stay unread; (d) when it sets gN to cancelled (all tickets cancelled, no tickets left, an open group closed with none left), every page of gN.

Case for (b): ticket #1, file .env-bad in the project (the fake preflight reports env): ticket_controller.py exits 3 with one env page of g1; remove .env-bad; the next run exits 0 with #1 landed and that env page acked as 'superseded'. (Today it stays unread: no path acks it.)

With devloop.remote naming a git remote whose push fails (added with a URL that does not exist), the push-failed decision page of g1 that landing writes stays unread.

## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
